meta.title: Data gaps: lawns and gardens, personal trainers, utilities by tariff, for eight SLATE cities

basis_legend.page: The figure was read from the source page or PDF itself (fetched or downloaded and text-extracted).
basis_legend.search-summary: The figure came from a web-search result summary and the page itself was not fetched. Treat it as a lead and verify before relying on it.
basis_legend.derived: Arithmetic on figures that are each sourced in the same entry; the arithmetic is shown.

meta.rule: No figure here was invented. Where nothing published was found, the value is null and a note says why.
builds_on: docs/research/world/research-utilities.json (providers, move-in costs, some tariff figures, read 2026-10-01)

measured.figure: 1.25 to 1.46 mm per day of canopy growth (without and with mulching mower), May 2022, perennial ryegrass / Kentucky bluegrass lawn mixture
measured.note: Grass and Forage Science paper, 'Response of Perennial Ryegrass/Kentucky Bluegrass Mixture to Mulching Mower Under Different Nitrogen Fertilisation Levels'. Late-spring figure; growth is slower in summer heat and autumn.

measured.figure: Turf clipping growth of 10.2 g per m2 per day in spring and 2 to 5 g per m2 per day in autumn (20:80 Kentucky bluegrass:perennial ryegrass mown to 55 mm)
measured.note: Dry-matter yield, not height. The spring rate is two to five times the autumn rate, which is the seasonal shape to model.

guidance.figure: Never remove more than one-third of leaf height at a mowing; at peak spring growth a lawn may need mowing more than once a week; mow at 2 inches or higher.
guidance.note: Penn State Extension. Publishes no growth rate in inches per week.

guidance.figure: Established cool-season turf about 1 inch (2.54 cm) per week under ideal conditions
guidance.note: Commercial blog, not research. It is 2.5 times the measured 1 cm per week above. Prefer the measured figure.

New York.frost_free: last spring frost about April 3, first fall frost about November 14, about 224 days (NOAA 1991-2020 normals, Central Park)
New York.note: Cool-season grass grows fastest in spring and autumn and slows in midsummer heat (Penn State page above). NYBG's reference desk gives Central Park's last freeze as April 1 to 15 and first frost around November 20: https://libanswers.nybg.org/faq/222609 (search-summary).

Los Angeles.note: UC IPM. Bermudagrass goes dormant in winter. Tall fescue lawns are also common in LA and grow most of the year. No frost-free figure was looked up, because frost is rare on the coastal basin.

New Haven.frost_free: last spring frost about April 22, first fall frost about October 20, about 180 days (NOAA 1991-2020 normals)

London.mowing_season: late March to late October; growth stops below about 5 C soil temperature; peak growth April to June and September to October

thermal_growing_season.figure: Central England thermal growing season (above 5.0 C daily mean) averaged 280 days in 2006-2015, against 252 days in 1961-1990
thermal_growing_season.note: Met Office analysis reported by Carbon Brief.

Dublin.figure: Grass grows in every month. Teagasc's PastureBase curve rises from January to a peak in mid-May; Irish summer (June to August) farm grass growth averages 50 to 65 kg DM per ha per day.
Dublin.note: These are farm pasture figures, not lawn height. No Irish lawn mowing-season figure was found.

Toronto.frost_free: last spring frost about April 20, first fall frost about November 1 (urban core), about 197 days (ECCC 1991-2020 normals)
Toronto.note: Third-party page computing from Environment and Climate Change Canada normals.

Vancouver.frost_free: last spring frost about March 15, first fall frost about November 30, about 260 days (ECCC 1991-2020 normals)

Mexico City.figure: Rainy season May to October (2026 season stated as 15 May to 15 November), wettest June to August
Mexico City.note: No published lawn growth or mowing figure for CDMX was found. The rainy season is the growth season by inference only, so the months are not a measured lawn figure.

United States.survey_year: 2025 annual averages, per the fetched table. A search summary gave the same figures as 2024, so check the year.
United States.note: Table 1 has no separate 'lawn, garden and houseplants' line; 'lawn and garden care' is the published line. Derived minutes = hours x 60, rounded.

United Kingdom.figure: 19 minutes per day on 'gardening and pet care', averaged over everyone (not only participants), UK excluding Scotland, 2014-15
DIY and gardening combined fell from 39 minutes per day (March 2020) to 10 minutes (March 2023), averaged over all adults

United Kingdom.note: No UK figure for minutes per day among people who gardened was found. The ONS figures are averages over everyone.

Canada.figure: About 11% of Canadians aged 30 and over did lawn or garden work on a typical day in 2005, and the average participant spent more than 2 hours on it
Canada.note: Statistics Canada, General Social Survey 2005. No later participant figure was found.

Ireland.note: No Irish time-use figure for gardening was found.

Mexico.note: Not searched in depth. INEGI's ENUT is the candidate source.

Toronto.rule: Owner or occupant must cut turfgrass whenever it exceeds 20 centimetres in height or length (s.489-2A). Land must be kept free of the local weeds listed in Schedule A, and growth must not block sidewalks or sight lines (s.489-2.1).
Toronto.enforcement: An officer may order compliance. If the order is not met, the City may enter and do the work at the person's expense (s.489-3.4).

fines.note: Daily fines may total more than $100,000. A special fine equal to any economic gain can be added. These are maximums on conviction, not set tickets.

Toronto.note: Chapter 489 was renamed 'Turfgrass and Prohibited Plants' by By-law 662-2021, in force 1 January 2022.

Vancouver.rule: Owners or occupiers must keep property clear of weeds, brush and other growth to a reasonable standard prevailing in the neighbourhood (Untidy Premises By-law No. 4548).

fines.continuing: same range for each day the offence continues

Vancouver.note: The PDF did not parse when downloaded. No height limit is stated.

New Haven.rule: Anti-Blight and Property Maintenance Ordinance caps grass and weeds at one foot (about 30 cm).
New Haven.abatement: If a violation dangerous to public health, safety or welfare is not corrected within 10 calendar days of written notice, the City may abate at the owner's expense.
New Haven.note: The city's Livable City Initiative page refused the fetch with HTTP 403.

Los Angeles.rule: Brush clearance (LAMC 57.1.603.5) applies in the Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone. Within 200 ft of structures and 10 ft of roads or combustible fences, grass must be cut to 3 inches, with compliance due by 1 May 2026. Separately, LAMC 56.08(a) bars vegetation that obstructs streets and sidewalks.

fees_usd_2026.plus: the contractor's lowest bid price, recovered as a special assessment and lien on the property tax bill

Los Angeles.note: This programme covers hillside and brush parcels. Flat-basin lawns have no city grass-height limit that was found. Unincorporated LA County charges a separate $59.07 weed inspection fee (https://file.lacounty.gov/SDSInter/bos/supdocs/213422.pdf, search-summary).

New York.rule: Health Code 181.11 bars an owner or occupant from allowing poison ivy, ragweed or other poisonous or allergenic weeds to grow on a lot. Admin Code 16-118 requires owners to keep sidewalks, and vacant lots, free of litter and debris.

sources.note: DSNY proposed raising the vacant-lot fine from $100 to $250.

New York.note: No NYC grass-height limit was found, and no penalty-schedule amount for 181.11 was found.

London.rule: Councils serve a Section 215 notice (Town and Country Planning Act 1990) when the condition of land harms the amenity of the area, which covers overgrown gardens. Failure to comply is an offence under s.216.

fines_england.first_conviction: a fine (unlimited) since the Levelling-up and Regeneration Act 2023, in force 25 April 2024
fines_england.daily_after_conviction: one-tenth of the greater of GBP 5,000 or level 4 on the standard scale, so at least GBP 500 a day

alternative_route.figure: Community Protection Notice. Breach can carry a fixed penalty of up to GBP 100 (GBP 85 if paid early, per some councils).

London.note: Level 4 is GBP 2,500 under the Criminal Justice Act 1982 s.37 (search-summary). A 2014 order to raise levels 1 to 4 appears in the search results, but whether it was ever made was not confirmed. The GBP 500 floor holds either way, because GBP 5,000 is the greater figure unless level 4 exceeds it.

Dublin.note: No Irish rule on grass height or overgrown gardens was found. The nearest instrument is the Derelict Sites Act 1990: an annual levy of 7% of market value on registered derelict sites, with interest of 1.25% a month on arrears. It targets dilapidated buildings, not untidy lawns.

Mexico City.rule: Ley de Cultura Civica de la Ciudad de Mexico, art. 28 fraccion XIII: an owner who fails to fence a vacant property, or to keep it free of pests or weeds (maleza) that can harm neighbours, commits an infraction.
Mexico City.class: C (art. 32 table: art. 28, fracciones V, VI, VII, VIII, X, XII, XIII, XIV and XIX)
Mexico City.penalty: Fine of 21 to 30 UMA, or 25 to 36 hours' arrest, or 12 to 18 hours' community work (art. 31)

sources.note: Text with the last reform published 15 June 2022.

Mexico City.note: The rule applies to inmuebles sin construccion (vacant lots), not to a garden at an occupied home.

studies.study: Storer TW, Dolezal BA, Berenc MN, Timmins JE, Cooper CB. J Strength Cond Res 2014;28(7):1995-2006
studies.design: RCT. Men aged 30-44, members of one Southern California fitness club, personal trainer (n=17) vs self-directed (n=17), 3 days a week for 12 weeks

results.lean_body_mass: +1.3 kg with trainer vs no change self-directed (p=0.029)

studies.effect_as_percent_difference: Chest press gain was 2.2 times as large (42 vs 19 percentage points; derived 42/19). Leg press gain was 1.5 times as large but not significant.
studies.basis_note: Abstract read through the Europe PMC API.

studies.study: Mazzetti SA, Kraemer WJ, Volek JS et al. Med Sci Sports Exerc 2000;32(6):1175-1184
studies.design: Moderately trained men aged 24.6, supervised by a personal trainer (n=10) vs unsupervised (n=8), identical 12-week linear periodized programme

results.summary: Weekly training loads were greater with supervision from week 7 (squat) and from weeks 3 and 7 (bench press). The rate of load increase was greater, and 1RM squat and bench press were significantly greater at week 12. Fat-free mass increased only in the supervised group.

studies.percent_gains_note: The abstract gives no percentages. The '30-45% more strength' figure circulating online (spectrumfit.net) is not in the abstract, so it is not recorded here.
studies.basis_note: Abstract read through the Europe PMC API.

studies.study: Coutts AJ, Murphy AJ, Dascombe BJ. J Strength Cond Res 2004;18(2):316-323
studies.design: Young rugby league players aged 16.7, supervised (n=21) vs unsupervised (n=21), 12 weeks

results.summary: The supervised group completed more sessions and gained more on 3RM squat (at 6 and 12 weeks) and 3RM bench (at 12 weeks). Percent gains in bench, squat and chin-ups were significantly greater.

studies.study: Coleman M, Burke R, ... Fisher JP, Vigotsky AD, Schoenfeld BJ. J Sports Sci 2023;41(12):1207-1217
studies.design: RCT, 36 resistance-trained young men and women, supervised vs unsupervised, 8 weeks, same programme

results.hypertrophy: Greater muscle thickness with supervision (triceps, all rectus femoris sites, proximal vastus lateralis)

studies.study: Gavanda S, Held S, Schrey S et al. J Strength Cond Res 2025;39(11):1129-1137
studies.design: RCT, 79 trained adults (48% women), 10 weeks, 3 sessions a week: in-person supervision (n=15) vs app coaching (n=39) vs self-guided PDF (n=25)

meta_analysis.study: Fisher J, Steele J et al. 2022, 'The Role of Supervision in Resistance Training; an Exploratory Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis', International Journal of Strength and Conditioning
meta_analysis.percent_note: Reported as a standardised effect, not as a percent.

personal_trainers_supervised_vs_unsuperv.synthesis_for_modelling: Across the trials with numbers, supervised training gave about 1.2 to 2.2 times the strength gain of unsupervised training on the same programme: +37% on squat (Gavanda 2025), 2.2 times on chest press (Storer 2014), and a pooled small effect, SMD 0.40 (Fisher 2022). Upper-body gains differed less in some trials (Coleman 2023 and Gavanda 2025 found none). Most of the benefit runs through adherence and load progression: unsupervised groups attend less and drop out more. Body-composition benefit is trivial in the meta-analysis.
